To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the best performing algorithm for network classification is Collective Classification with a Random Walk (CCRW), (ii) the second best performing algorithm is Collective Classification with Label Propagation (CCLP), and (iii) the worst performing algorithm is Collective Inference with a Markov Random Field (CIMRF).
(1) the best algorithm depends on the network structure and (2) the best algorithm for a specific network depends on the number of classes.

(i) the performance of the four inference algorithms varies significantly depending on the network data and (ii) in general, the performance of the inference algorithms improves as the network data becomes sparser.
